notes: First-time DTC extraction, no precedent (per BRIEF). ACCESS: robots.txt (https://www.muuto.com/robots.txt) has only a generic User-agent:* group with no Claude-specific disallow -- direct fetch worked for every page, no WAF/bot-block encountered, Rule 2 escalation not needed. SITE ARCHITECTURE: Muuto is furniture-first (Seating/Sofas/Tables/Storage all excluded per brief). Category pages are server-rendered Vue with a client PLP component (tile-filter) backed by a same-origin JSON endpoint /api/products?pageId=<id>; used this for exact, exhaustion-checked leaf counts (results array length = 'hits' = number of distinct master products/tiles, cross-verified against raw SSR <product-tile master-id=...> tag counts on 3 categories -- vases, mirrors, kitchen -- which matched exactly). QTY VERIFICATION (Rule 1): the API also returns a 'totalHits' field which is consistently HIGHER than 'hits' on several categories (e.g. Wall Lamps hits=9/totalHits=17, Table Lamps hits=14/totalHits=18, Floor Lamps hits=7/totalHits=11, Candleholders hits=2/totalHits=4) -- this totalHits figure counts underlying finished-good/SKU variants (colors/sizes), not distinct products, and is the same kind of inflated aggregate this project has repeatedly found in Shopify/Magento/Searchspring counts, so it was NOT used. Used 'hits' (= enumerated distinct master product count, matching the actual rendered tile grid) as qty throughout. Special case: Candleholders -- SSR grid + API both show only 2 live master products (Pair Candleholder, Float Candlestick) though the page's own UI badge text '${availableTotalResults} items' is bound to the inflated totalHits=4; a search for the 3rd facet value 'The More The Merrier' (visible only in the Family facet list) returns hits:0/totalHits:1 via the same endpoint, i.e. a retired/unavailable product family still lingering in facet metadata -- treated the empirically enumerable count (2) as authoritative. RULE 0 GAINS: included Hangers (7: Avail/Attach/Coil coat hooks & racks, plus the 'Dots' ceramic/metal/wood wall-hook collection) under Decorative Accessories per Rule-adjacent brief text explicitly listing 'hooks, racks' as in-scope decorative metal items -- this category is easy to misclassify as excluded 'storage' but the product type is decorative wall hooks, not furniture storage. EXCLUSIONS CHECKED AND DROPPED (mixed roll-ups / facet re-cuts, not padded): Accessories>Storage (15 items) and Accessories>Office (11 items) and top-level Storage>Small Storage (12 items) are all overlapping room-view re-cuts of the same organizational furniture/storage-accessory product IDs (baskets, shelving, toolbox, bookends, pinboard) -- majority excluded storage/furniture, and the few decorative tray/bowl IDs that leak into these lists (Wave Tray, Platform Tray, Mere Bowl) are already captured once under Kitchen, so not double-counted. Rugs, Cushions, Throws (Accessories) dropped as textiles (explicit exclusion). Outdoor>Accessories (7 items) checked and dropped: entirely composed of excluded items (Settle Cushion textile, Outdoor Cover, Linear Steel bar stool/bench seat pad, Ply Rug) plus 2 portable lamps (Ease Portable Lamp, Beam Portable Lamp) that are already counted once under Table Lamps -- no unique decor items found there. Shop-by-Family facet menu (Ambit, Dots, Fine Lamp, Linear Steel/System, etc.) is a pure design-line re-cut of products already listed under Lighting/Accessories -- skipped per Rule 0.6. 'Show all Lighting' / 'Show all Accessories' / 'All products' are aggregator pages, never extracted per brief; Lighting has no separate room-based tree (only a lamp-type tree: Floor/Pendant/Table/Wall), so Rule 0.1's room-traversal requirement is satisfied by the type tree already being exhaustive per the site's own nav. Some lamp master IDs appear in two type leaves (e.g. Dedicate in both Floor and Table Lamps as different configurations, Looped/Fine in both Pendant and Wall) -- reported each leaf's own site-verified count as-is, not deduplicated across leaves, consistent with how the site itself buckets them.
